title: First light
text: Land pushed up out of the water and the sea settled around it. Trees took root on the slopes, and twenty-six small wanderers set off walking. A sun and a moon began their circles overhead.

title: The world finds its poles
text: Cold gathered at the top and bottom of the world. Ice closed over the far north and south, and the sea went pale and still around it. Between the ice and the warm middle a line appeared that the forests will not cross — above it, bare tundra; just below it, dark narrow firs holding on. Down near the equator the leaves came in broader and brighter. The trees have begun to move in the wind.

title: Weather
text: The first clouds gathered. They sit in a loose deck a little way above the ground, throwing no shadow yet, drifting always the same way around the world. Near the equator they hurry; up toward the ice they barely move at all, so the whole sky slowly pulls itself apart and gathers again. The highest peaks stand clear above them.

title: Shadows on the ground
text: The clouds began to fall on the world below them. Each one now carries a soft dark patch across the land and the water, always on the side away from the sun, sliding over hills and out to sea as the day turns. Where the sun stands overhead a cloud sits squarely on its own shadow; toward evening the two draw apart, and the shadows thin away into the dusk.

title: The wanderers keep hours
text: Until now the sun rose and set over creatures who never noticed. That has changed. As the light leaves a place its wanderers settle where they stand, lower themselves to the ground and sleep, breathing slowly, until it comes back. They do not all wake at once — some are up before the sun has properly cleared the horizon, others lie in a while longer. Through the middle of the day they range furthest. There are more of them now, too, so the line between the sleeping half of the world and the waking half is easy to find.
